title: Binary Tree Paths
summary: Provide all paths from the tree's root to its leaf nodes, listed in any order.
statement: Provide all paths from the tree's root to its leaf nodes, listed in any order. A leaf node is defined as a node with no child nodes.
constraints: root contains 1–100 TreeNode objects with values from -100 through 100.
Return every root-to-leaf path as values joined by '->'. A leaf has neither child; output order does not matter.

hints: A result is recorded only at a node with no left child and no right child.
Carry the current sequence of value strings through depth-first recursion.
Append the node value, recurse into existing children, then pop it while backtracking.
Join and save a copy only at leaves; otherwise shared mutable path state can leak between branches.
editorial: Depth-first recursion mirrors the path definition. The current list contains exactly the nodes from root to the active node. A leaf records that list as one arrow-joined string; popping restores the parent's path before another branch. The independent oracle represents nodes by binary paths and constructs each leaf result from its path prefixes.
